question: What defines a pharmaceutical suspension?

options.A: Solid drug particles dispersed in a liquid vehicle
options.B: A completely clear solution of dissolved chemical salts
options.C: An oily substance bound permanently to water molecules
options.D: A solid tablet compressed with binding agents

explanation: Suspensions contain undissolved solid particles floating throughout a liquid medium rather than fully dissolving. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h1)

question: Why might a nurse need to dilute a medicinal suspension?

options.A: To speed up the chemical expiration date of the drug
options.B: To turn the liquid preparation back into a dry powder
options.C: To permanently dissolve the solid particles completely
options.D: To fit a lower prescribed dose or clear a feeding tube

explanation: Diluting alters concentration and volume, making it easier to measure tiny doses or pass viscous fluids through narrow tubing. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h1)

question: What formula guides basic drug dilution calculations?

options.C: BSA = square root of H times W

explanation: The concentration-volume equation is the standard mathematical tool for calculating fluid dilutions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h2)

question: What is the very first step in calculating a drug dilution?

options.A: Identify the stock strength on the manufacturer label
options.B: Add sterile water directly to the powder container
options.C: Calculate the patient body surface area in square meters
options.D: Discard half of the bottle contents into the sink

explanation: You must first know the baseline concentration of the medication before performing any dilution math. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which measuring tool should a nurse NEVER use for liquid medications?
explanation: Household spoons lack standardization and cause severe dosing errors. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h3)

question: Why is tap water discouraged when reconstituting oral medications?

options.A: It changes the color of the plastic measuring cup
options.B: It may introduce microbes and mineral impurities
options.C: It freezes the liquid suspension instantly
options.D: It reacts chemically to turn the drug into a gas

explanation: Sterile or purified water is required to maintain microbiological safety and chemical stability. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h3)

question: What action must be performed immediately before measuring a suspension?

options.A: Add a drop of food coloring to check viscosity
options.B: Shake the container vigorously to re-suspend settled particles
options.C: Filter the liquid through a paper gauze pad
options.D: Heat the bottle in a microwave for thirty seconds

explanation: Suspensions settle over time, so shaking ensures the dose drawn is representative of the whole mixture. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h4)

question: What is a mandatory final step after preparing a diluted medication?

options.A: Label the container with the new concentration and date
options.B: Taste the mixture to verify the sweetness level
options.C: Leave the syringe sitting uncapped on the bedside table
options.D: Store the open container in direct sunlight

explanation: Clear labeling prevents accidental administration errors from misidentifying altered drug concentrations. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h4)

question: What environmental condition is commonly required for many diluted liquid antibiotics?

options.A: Freezing below minus 20°C in a deep chest freezer
options.B: Storage inside a sealed, unventilated metal box
options.C: Direct placement on a warm window ledge in the sun

explanation: Many liquid antibiotic suspensions lose stability quickly at room temperature and must be kept cold. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h5)

question: Which sign indicates that a diluted suspension is unsafe to administer?

options.A: Clear legible handwriting on the preparation label
options.B: A cool temperature felt upon touching the glass bottle
options.C: Permanent caking and unyielding sediment at the bottom
options.D: A uniform milky appearance after gentle swirling

explanation: Hard caking that refuses to redisperse shows chemical breakdown or improper storage, making the dose unreliable. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h5)
